{4,24,-22} at 0.801 remains the best. This is well below the search-adjusted bar (1.021), which accounts for multiple-testing/overfitting given how many specs I could try. I've done a fairly thorough search across all 40 singles, many pairs, and many triples around the best candidates without finding anything close to clearing the bar. Given the difficulty of exceeding it, I'll settle on this best-found specification and submit with a conservative, appropriately-calibrated OOS belief (well below the in-sample Sharpe, reflecting the multiple-testing haircut implied by the bar).

I submitted the specification **{feature 4 (long), feature 24 (long), feature 22 (short)}**, equal-weighted.

**Summary of my process:**
1. Evaluated all 40 individual features long — best was ~0.41 (features 4, 24).
2. Searched pairwise combinations among the strongest singles — best pair (4+24) reached 0.581.
3. Searched triples by adding a third feature to the best pair, including short-sign variants — discovered {4, 24, −22} at **0.801 Sharpe in-sample**, a notable nonlinear synergy since 4+22 and 24+22 alone were both weak (~0.55).
4. Extensively tried replacing each leg of this triple with all other features and sign flips (~90+ additional evaluations) — nothing beat 0.801.

**Why my submitted belief is conservative:** The tool reported a "search-adjusted bar" of ~1.021 that accounts for the multiple-testing inherent in searching many specifications — my best in-sample Sharpe (0.801) never cleared it. This is a strong signal that some of the 0.801 is likely search/overfitting noise rather than genuine signal. I therefore submitted a predicted out-of-sample Sharpe with mean 0.25 and sd 0.35 — substantially haircut from the in-sample value, reflecting realistic uncertainty about how much of that performance will persist out-of-sample.
